findings.claim: The Holistic / Systemic value grounded in Deming and Goldratt refuses the resource-allocation framing of stakeholders; people are constitutive of the system, not inputs to it.
findings.failure_mode: The source says people are part of the system 'not just as resources, but also as full rounded individuals'; the 'not just ... but also' keeps the resource view and adds to it. The distillation turns this into a refusal of the resource framing, contradicting the quotation it has just given. Recurs at 59 ('treated as inputs to a system or as constitutive parts of it?'), 138 ('puts people inside the system, not as inputs') and 162 ('Treating people as resources — Open Kanban's ... value refuses this; people constitute the system, they are not inputs to it').
findings.evidence: Deep 52: 'And the key part of the system is people, not just as resources, but also as full rounded individuals who make the system work' [V] ('Open Kanban Values'). Source line 100.
findings.fix: correct: The Holistic / Systemic value asks that people be seen not only as resources but as full rounded individuals who make the system work. (At 162: 'Treating people only as resources — Open Kanban's value asks that they also be seen as full rounded individuals who make the system work.')

findings.claim: The Mitchell-Agle-Wood salience model (power, legitimacy, urgency) provides the stakeholder-mapping theory Open Kanban lacks.
findings.failure_mode: The Business Ethics deep ref's Ch 3 uses the Donaldson-Preston taxonomy and the Grunig-Hunt linkage model; the Mitchell-Agle-Wood salience model is absent from it and from every deep ref in the corpus.
findings.evidence: openstax-business-ethics-deep 101-117 (Ch 3: Donaldson and Preston descriptive/instrumental/normative [BT]; Grunig-Hunt four stakeholder categories [BT]). grep 'salience', 'Agle' across all deep refs: no stakeholder-model hits.
findings.fix: correct: OpenStax Business Ethics Ch 3 (stakeholder definition and prioritisation: Donaldson-Preston's descriptive/instrumental/normative taxonomy and Grunig-Hunt's four stakeholder categories) provides the stakeholder-mapping theory Open Kanban lacks.

findings.claim: names *people* as "the key part of the system" [V] — not as resources but as "full rounded individuals who make the system work." [V]
findings.failure_mode: The unquoted connective 'not as resources but as' drops the source's 'just ... also', turning 'not just as resources, but also as' into a rejection of the resource view.
findings.evidence: Deep 52 [V]; source line 100: 'not just as resources, but also as full rounded individuals'.
findings.fix: correct: names *people* as "the key part of the system" [V], "not just as resources, but also as full rounded individuals who make the system work" [V].

findings.claim: The information radiator ... is the engagement-enabling artefact: it makes the work visible to anyone who walks past.
findings.failure_mode: Outside gloss (Cockburn's own definition); the source says 'signs and diagrams that the team can see in their work environment'. Recurs at 34 ('Any stakeholder who walks past sees the work') and 125.
findings.evidence: Deep 62: 'one can also use signs and diagrams that the team can see in their work environment, like dashboards, performance metrics or other information radiators' [V].
findings.fix: correct: it puts the work where the team can see it in their work environment; placed where stakeholders pass, it serves them too.

findings.claim: Open Kanban's "Movement" framing — modelled on the Free Software Movement's four freedoms
findings.failure_mode: Misnamed lineage: the source says it is 'inspired by the Open Source movement goal to give software users and developers the four essential freedoms of free software'.
findings.fix: correct: Open Kanban's "Movement" framing — inspired by the open-source movement's goal of the four essential freedoms of free software

findings.claim: The framework deliberately refuses to require a precondition (formal restructuring) it cannot guarantee.
findings.failure_mode: Supplies a rationale the source does not give.
findings.evidence: Deep 66, 152: 'Kanban starts where you are, and does not need to modify any titles or roles' [V]; no reason given.
findings.fix: correct: The framework does not require formal restructuring: Kanban 'starts where you are'.

findings.claim: *Muri* (overburden) destroys engagement; sustainable pace protects it.
findings.failure_mode: Outside-knowledge gloss: the source pairs Muri with Agile's sustainable pace and never translates it as overburden. Recurs at 68, 99, 141, 161 ('*Muri* (overburden) ... is the named failure mode').
findings.evidence: Deep 29: 'Respect for people also aligns with sustainable pace in Agile, or Muri 無理 in Lean' [V]; deep 154. 'overburden' absent from deep ref and source.
findings.fix: correct: Exhaustion destroys engagement; the sustainable pace the source pairs with Lean's *Muri* protects it.

findings.claim: "We only ask you that you: Give us credit; Contribute your best ideas back to Open Kanban root repository." (no marker)
findings.failure_mode: Verbatim quotation without [V]; same at line 59 ('People... [are] not just as resources, but also as full rounded individuals who make the system work.').

findings.section: Questions, Phase 3 (Use the Kanban board as conversation anchor)
findings.claim: Open Kanban's collaboration claim is that the board is the artefact that organises the conversation.
findings.failure_mode: Overstates the source: the board 'makes it easier to collaborate in a team setting' and 'provides transparency'; the source does not say it organises conversations.
findings.fix: correct: Open Kanban's claim is that the board makes it easier to collaborate and gives everyone transparency about the work.

findings.section: Questions, Phase 3 (Treat the manager as collaborator)
findings.claim: "Manager you can easily see at any moment what is the status of things, and if you are a team member you can see your impact on the overall work." [V]
findings.failure_mode: Quotation marked [V] is not word for word: the source reads 'If you are a manager you can easily see ...'; 'Manager you can easily see' is not in the source.
findings.evidence: Deep 62; source line 109: 'If you are a manager you can easily see at any moment what is the status of things'.
findings.fix: correct: "If you are a manager you can easily see at any moment what is the status of things, and if you are a team member you can see your impact on the overall work." [V]

findings.section: What to Look For, repeated retrospective ideas
findings.claim: The fourth practice — Learn and improve continuously — requires the same pull discipline as the first three.
findings.failure_mode: Attributes a requirement the source does not state; pull is tied to the Respect value, not to the first three practices.
findings.evidence: Deep 27 (demand-pull under Respect for people); deep 56-87 (four practices; none states pull discipline for the fourth).
findings.fix: correct: Treat improvement ideas like any other work: put them on the board and pull them.

findings.section: Anti-patterns, Engagement without a learning close
findings.claim: An engagement cycle that closes without a Retrospective, Strategy Meeting, or Kaizen Group has not closed its learning loop.
findings.failure_mode: Treats three named forms as necessary; the source lists them as examples among 'many ways'.
findings.evidence: Deep 85 [V]; deep 158 ('optional examples among many ways').
findings.fix: correct: An engagement cycle that closes with no learning step (a Retrospective, Strategy Meeting, Kaizen Group, or another form) has not closed its learning loop.

findings.section: Anti-patterns, CC BY 3.0 licence as an excuse
findings.claim: treating the licence permissiveness as permission to extract without contributing is the named failure mode.
findings.failure_mode: The source names no such failure mode; it asks for contribution back and the licence permits keeping forks private.
findings.evidence: Deep 108: 'We only ask you that you: Give us credit; Contribute your best ideas back' [V]; 'contribute back is named as a request, not a licence requirement ... a fork-and-keep-private outcome is permitted'.
findings.fix: correct: the licence permits using without contributing back, but the source asks for contribution back; extracting without contributing runs against its stated preference.

findings.section: Integration, NHS Just Culture and LFUO
findings.claim: Open Kanban motivates the person to surface an issue; Just Culture and LFUO protect them when they do.
findings.failure_mode: The NHS guide evaluates staff involved in a patient safety incident, not people who raise issues; LFUO's Just Culture principle concerns the response to unintended outcomes. Neither deep ref frames itself as protecting the person who surfaces an issue.
findings.evidence: nhs-just-culture-guide-deep 17 [V] ('whether a staff member involved in a patient safety incident requires specific individual support or intervention'); lfuo-learning-review-guide-2024-deep 7, 15 (Just Culture as a response to unintended outcomes).
findings.fix: correct: Open Kanban asks lower-rank people to name mistakes by those in authority; NHS Just Culture and LFUO steer the response to incidents away from blaming individuals. Use both layers when designing conditions for upward correction.

findings.section: Citation and Source-Integrity Notes, Evidence-marker continuity
findings.claim: uses `[V]`, `[AR]`, and `[BT]` markers throughout (48 `[V]`, 23 `[BT]`, 2 `[AR]`). This distillation paraphrases except for quotations marked `[V]`, which match the source word for word
findings.failure_mode: Count wrong and self-audit inaccurate: the deep ref carries 66 [V], 23 [BT], 2 [AR] and 1 [AP]; the [V] quotation at line 79 is not word for word, and two verbatim quotations (42, 59) lack [V].
findings.evidence: grep counts on open-kanban-deep.md: [V] 66, [BT] 23, [AR] 2, [AP] 1. Distillation lines 42, 59, 79.
findings.fix: correct: uses `[V]`, `[AP]`, `[AR]` and `[BT]` markers (66 `[V]`, 23 `[BT]`, 2 `[AR]`, 1 `[AP]`). [Fix lines 42, 59, 79 so every verbatim quotation carries [V] and matches the source.]

notes: The cleanest of the five open-kanban distillations: it carries no imported constraint/throughput frame, and it flags its own limits well (line 8 says the source does not name stakeholder engagement; lines 193-198 list what it does not develop). Apart from line 79, all [V] quotations match the converted source (line 24 inserts a [BT] marker inside the quotation; line 32 inserts '[are]'). The line 153 statement 'No verbatim source blockquotes appear' is literally true (inline quotations, no '>' blockquotes). Integration rows verified: Letaw (Tuckman, fist of five, RACI, ground rules, elicitation, paper prototyping, Inclusivity Heuristics), OB Chs 9-14 topics, TC 25-20 horseshoe seating and rank-consciousness passage (deep 221), SSDL feedback and accumulations briefs. The Worked Example's 'Courage value fires' when an analyst flags a regulation conflict stretches the source's upward-correction sense but is scenario, not graded.
